module.title: Production Security Engineering
module.description: Learn how professional applications protect systems, users, APIs, infrastructure, and data from real-world security threats.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Security engineering protects applications, infrastructure, users, and data from attacks and vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Are Constant Targets
sections.content: Public applications face attacks continuously from bots, hackers, malicious scripts, and automated systems.

sections.heading: Security Is Infrastructure
sections.content: Authentication, APIs, databases, payments, uploads, and cloud systems all require protection.

sections.heading: One Vulnerability Can Destroy Systems
sections.content: Small security mistakes can expose user accounts, private data, or entire infrastructure.

sections.heading: Professional Engineering Prioritizes Security
sections.content: Production engineering always considers security during architecture and development.

easyExample.title: Bank Security Example
easyExample.content: Banks use guards, cameras, vaults, and verification systems together instead of relying on one lock.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: XSS attacks inject malicious scripts into applications to steal data or manipulate users.

sections.heading: How XSS Works
sections.content: Attackers inject JavaScript into vulnerable applications where other users unknowingly execute it.

sections.heading: Frontend Security Risks
sections.content: Unsafe rendering and user-generated content often create XSS vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: Stolen Sessions And Data
sections.content: XSS can steal cookies, tokens, and sensitive user information.

sections.heading: Professional Frontend Protection
sections.content: Modern frameworks and sanitization systems help reduce XSS risks.

easyExample.title: Fake Announcement Example
easyExample.content: A malicious fake school announcement tricks students into revealing information.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: SQL injection attacks manipulate database queries using malicious input.

sections.heading: Unsafe Queries Create Risks
sections.content: Applications that directly combine user input into database queries become vulnerable.

sections.heading: Attackers Manipulate Databases
sections.content: SQL injection can expose, modify, or delete sensitive information.

sections.heading: Parameterized Queries
sections.content: Professional systems safely separate data from executable queries.

sections.heading: Database Security Is Critical
sections.content: Production applications heavily protect database access and queries.

easyExample.title: Fake Security Badge Example
easyExample.content: Someone tricks a guard using fake credentials to access restricted areas.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Authentication and API security protect user accounts, sessions, and backend infrastructure.

sections.heading: APIs Are Public Attack Targets
sections.content: Attackers constantly test APIs for weak authentication and authorization.

sections.heading: Token Security
sections.content: JWTs, refresh tokens, and secure cookies require careful handling.

sections.heading: Authorization Checks
sections.content: Professional systems verify permissions for every protected operation.

sections.heading: Production Authentication Engineering
sections.content: Large systems combine rate limiting, session management, and layered security.

easyExample.title: Airport Passport Example
easyExample.content: Airports verify both identity and travel permissions before allowing access.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Rate limiting controls request frequency to protect systems from abuse and overload.

sections.heading: Public APIs Face Abuse
sections.content: Attackers and bots can flood applications with massive numbers of requests.

sections.heading: Rate Limiting Systems
sections.content: Applications restrict how many requests users can make within specific time periods.

sections.heading: DDOS Attacks
sections.content: Distributed attacks overwhelm infrastructure using huge traffic floods.

sections.heading: Infrastructure Protection
sections.content: Professional systems combine firewalls, CDNs, and traffic filtering.

easyExample.title: Concert Entry Example
easyExample.content: Security limits how many people enter at once to prevent dangerous overcrowding.

definition.title: Simple Definition
definition.content: Production security engineering focuses on building layered defenses protecting infrastructure, applications, users, and distributed systems.

sections.heading: Security Is Continuous
sections.content: Production systems face constant attacks, scanning, abuse, and automated threats.

sections.heading: Modern Applications Require Layered Security
sections.content: Authentication, APIs, databases, infrastructure, cloud systems, and frontend applications all require protection.

sections.heading: Professional Security Engineering
sections.content: Large companies prioritize monitoring, vulnerability prevention, traffic filtering, and access control.

sections.heading: Thinking Beyond Simple Passwords
sections.content: Professional engineers think about infrastructure resilience, attack prevention, and system-wide security architecture.

easyExample.title: Military Base Example
easyExample.content: Military bases use gates, guards, cameras, alarms, checkpoints, and restricted zones together for layered protection.

basicCode.title: Production Security Flow
basicCode.code: User → CDN → Firewall → Rate Limiter → Auth System → API → Database
